Model: fixed x in {0,1}^n, free set F of size k chosen uniformly, bottom gate threshold t uniform on the window {lo..hi} of its weighted sum. structure.text: DISCOVERY cm-9ccf99e0ef5d4d4e (own code, n = s = 2^k, k = 12..20, l = s^2, d = l/(100 s log2 s) asserted >= 2 on every row, h = n/log2 l). Hypotheses: H1 log2 L / log2 s bounded (poly-in-s unfolding); H2 log2 L ~ n/2 (exponential). Predicted H2. Result: MATCHED H2. log2 L / n rises 0.074 -> 0.226 (k=12..20); log2 L / log2 s grows 25 -> 11841. Closed form (n/2)(1 - log2(100 log2 s)/log2 s) matches the computed values exactly. Analytic consequence: for any s >= n in the Lemma 3.1 regime, log2 L = n/2 - o(n), so the naive top-tree unfolding gives about 2^{n/2} = sqrt(N) leaves, not poly(s). Scope: leaf count of the top tree only, under the stated fan-in/depth parameters from the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 source check (7703b13cb4f84d2d). Void: cm-21d481f7ccc341b3 clamped d to 2 and is not evidence. Does NOT close G0001: it shows the naive unfolding is exponential, but whether a formula lower bound at s = poly(n) contradicts sqrt(N) is open.

statement: FAST EVALUATION - COUNTEREXAMPLE found by independent computation to the claim: For any family F of 3-element clauses over GF(3) variables, let cov(F) be the number of variables appearing in F, and rank(F) the GF(3) rank of its incidence matrix. If F is 'blind' (meaning: (a) F is 1-in-3 unsatisfiable over {0,1}, and (b) the all-1 vector is not in the row space of the incidence matrix over GF(3)), then rank(F) = min(cov(F) - 1, |F|). | The family F = {{0,1,4}, {0,2,4}, {0,3,4}, {1,2,3}} is blind: it is 1-in-3 unsatisfiable (x1=x2=x3 forces 3·x1=1) and the all-ones vector is not in its GF(3) row space. Its GF(3) rank is 3 (R4 = R3 − R2), but the claim requires min(cov−1, |F|) = min(4, 4) = 4.

statement: CG RANK 1 FOR ALL UNSAT POSITIVE 1-IN-3 FORMULAS ON <= 7 VARIABLES - decided exactly (director, 2026-11-19; scripts /root/fruits/research/PNP-001/lab/review-2026-11-19/gapcores.py + cgrank7.py). Reduction (proved): every UNSAT formula contains a minimal UNSAT subformula M; if M is GF(3)-inconsistent it has no integer solution and one CG round refutes it (D-023); otherwise M is a minimal GAP core; supersets only shrink the first CG closure; x = 1/3 is always LP-feasible (D-016h), so the rank is >= 1. Computation: all 62,370 minimal GAP cores on 7 labelled variables (includes those on <= 6 used variables) were enumerated exactly; for EACH, exact rational vertex enumeration of P = {Ax = 1, 0 <= x <= 1} (<= 2 free dimensions by T44 C4) finds a variable j with 0 < min_P x_j and max_P x_j < 1, so the CG cuts x_j >= 1 and x_j <= 0 refute it in one round: 60,480 cores with 1 free dimension, 1,890 with 2 (= the owner's two support-nullity-2 classes, 1,260 + 630), 0 without certificate. Result: CG rank exactly 1. Finite theorem; says nothing about n >= 8 or about the cost of FINDING the cuts.

statement: FAST EVALUATION - independently recomputed and CONFIRMED on the stated finite domain only (not a proof of any general statement): The positive 1-in-3 formula with clauses {x0,x1,x2}, {x0,x1,x3}, {x0,x1,x4}, {x2,x3,x4} on variables x0..x4 is unsatisfiable, and its GF(3) incidence matrix has rank 3. Hence 'GF(3) incidence rank <= 4 implies satisfiable' is false. Derivation: if x0=1 then x1=x2=x3=x4=0, so clause {x2,x3,x4} sums to 0; if x0=0 then x2=x3=x4=1-x1, so {x2,x3,x4} sums to 0 or 3, never 1. | scope: Exactly this one formula (n=5, 4 clauses). Not a claim about any other n or formula. | evaluator: The formula is UNSAT (0 satisfying assignments over all 32 assignments, confirmed by hand and by a drat-trim-verified refutation), and its GF(3) rank is 3 (confirmed by two independent computations), so the rank ≤ 4 ⇒ satisfiable implication is refuted by this instance.

statement: Smith normal forms over Z on the 1350 GF(3)-consistent blind positive 3-clause sets on 6 variables (m=5,6,7). Of the 30 integer-infeasible sets (all m=6), SNF(A) = (1,1,1,1,1,9) and SNF([A|1]) = (1,1,1,1,1,3): the invariant factors differ by a factor exactly 3, and the only non-unit factor is a power of 3. This supports the factor-3 half of D-023 (differ only by 3) on n=6 and locates the integer obstruction in the 3-part. The literature identity tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1)-1 is still unverified: no source has been checked, so no novelty claim is made.
